implementation_notes: MRI micro-optimisation is also mostly a category error - the interpreter's method dispatch and object allocation dominate - so the real answer on CRuby 3.x is YJIT (which JIT-compiles hot methods, so the micro-optimisation becomes getting the code hot and shape-stable) or moving the hot code to a C extension. Profile with ruby-prof or stackprof, and measure with benchmark-ips (which handles GC and warm-up). The micro-optimisations that pay in MRI are allocation reduction (which YJIT can then remove), the packed numeric buffers from the array gem (Array of Floats boxes every element; pack('f*') into a String is contiguous), and avoiding method calls in a loop. On JRuby, YJIT does not apply and the JIT compiles the whole program, so the Java-level techniques (shape stability, avoiding megamorphic sites) apply instead.
idiom_name: stackprof / ruby-prof attribution plus benchmark-ips; on CRuby 3.x enable YJIT, then micro-optimise shape stability and allocation
code_sketch:
# CRuby 3.x: enable YJIT first - the JIT removes much of what you would
# hand-optimise. Then the wins are shape stability and allocation.
#   ruby --yjit app.rb
#
# 1. PROFILE: ruby-prof (sampling) or stackprof (fast, low overhead)
# 2. BOUND: if the hotspot is 4%, Amdahl caps the win at 4%.
# 3. ONE CHANGE at the measured hotspot. The MRI wins:
#    - the array gem's packed buffer (Array of Floats boxes each element;
#      pack('f*') is a contiguous String):
require 'array'
buf = Array.new(n, 0.0)
packed = buf.pack('f*')            # contiguous, machine-speed numeric work
#    - shape stability so YJIT's inline caches stay monomorphic
#    - fewer method calls per iteration (the dispatch dominates in MRI)
# 4. VERIFY with benchmark-ips (handles warm-up and GC):
#    ruby -Ilib -rbenchmark/ips bench.rb
# 5. GUARD: keep the benchmark in CI.
# NOTE: on JRuby the JIT compiles the whole program, so the Java-level
#       techniques (monomorphic sites, no boxing) apply instead.
pitfalls: Micro-optimising MRI's interpreter dispatch is a few percent at best; enable YJIT (CRuby 3.x) or move the hot code to a C extension.
An Array of Floats boxes every element in MRI; the array gem's packed buffer is the contiguous, machine-speed equivalent.
Shape instability defeats YJIT's inline caches the same way it does in JavaScript - build objects consistently.
A hand-rolled timing loop measures the timer and the GC; benchmark-ips handles warm-up and reports statistics.
On JRuby there is no GVL and YJIT does not apply; the JIT compiles everything, so the optimisation targets are different.
